tracks.title: Data Engineering for Chemistry
tracks.tagline: Chemical data you can trust: databases, pipelines, validation, scale and monitoring.
tracks.summary: Three series that take chemical data from loose files to production pipelines: first the engineering itself, built by hand (Series 1), then the industry tools that run it at scale (Series 2), then the data side of automated and autonomous chemistry (Series 3).

series.title: Data Engineering for Cheminformatics
series.tagline: From SDF files to chemical data pipelines that scale to millions of molecules, survive failures and can be trusted.
series.level: For chemists who know some Python
series.summary: Fifteen modules on the engineering that sits between raw chemical files and machine learning. It starts with how molecules are represented and stored, in relational and graph databases; then the course turns to what breaks in practice: libraries too big for memory, jobs that need many cores, pipelines that fail halfway, data that drifts, and results nobody can reproduce. Each idea is built by hand first, so you understand it before Series 2 hands it to industry tools.

modules.title: Molecules as graphs and matrices
modules.what: A molecule is a graph: atoms are nodes, bonds are edges. Build it in NetworkX, write it as adjacency, bond-order and distance matrices, encode atom and bond properties (weights, one-hot features, bond tensors, edge lists), and compute on it with NumPy, up to one step of message passing.

modules.title: Molecules as text, patterns and numbers
modules.what: SMILES (canonical and isomeric), InChI and InChIKey, molfiles and SDF, 3D conformers, SMARTS patterns, fingerprints and descriptors: what each keeps, what each loses (stereochemistry, tautomers, aromaticity), and which to store for which job.

modules.title: Chemical files and identity
modules.what: The files molecules travel in (SDF, SMILES, CSV, Parquet), what each costs in space and time, and a stable identity for every molecule (InChIKey) so duplicates can be found.

modules.title: A chemical database
modules.what: Load a library into PostgreSQL with the RDKit cartridge, index it, search by substructure and similarity, read query plans, and use DuckDB for fast analysis.

modules.title: Molecules as graphs, and graph databases
modules.what: A molecule is a graph: atoms are nodes, bonds are edges. Work with it as one (rings, paths, substructure as subgraph matching, maximum common substructure), then store chemistry in a graph database: molecules linked to reactions, targets and assays, queried with Cypher. Compare it with the relational database and see where each one wins.

modules.title: Validating molecules
modules.what: Catch broken structures before they spread: parsing and sanitisation errors, impossible valences, unexpected elements and charges, missing or contradictory stereochemistry, size limits; decide what to fix, what to reject and how to record why.

modules.title: Standardisation as a tested transformation
modules.what: Strip salts, neutralise charges and choose one tautomer as a pure, deterministic function with versioned rules and unit tests.

modules.title: Libraries larger than memory
modules.what: Stream molecules in batches instead of loading them all, write partitioned Parquet, and query far more rows than fit in memory; measure memory and throughput as you go.

modules.title: Parallel and distributed processing
modules.what: Spread standardisation and fingerprints across cores with joblib, then across memory and machines with Dask: chunk sizes, passing SMILES instead of molecule objects, when parallel work stops helping, and a scaling curve; the same code on Windows, macOS and Linux.

modules.title: Pipelines that survive failure
modules.what: Idempotent steps, checkpoints and cached results, resuming from the last good batch, retries with back-off, atomic writes, quarantining bad molecules instead of crashing, and settings checked before a run starts.

modules.title: Incremental ingestion from ChEMBL and PubChem
modules.what: Fetch only what changed, page through APIs within their rate limits, cache responses, check every response against a model so a changed API fails loudly, and run backfills safely.

modules.title: Validating data: records with Pydantic, tables with Pandera
modules.what: Check single records at the edges with Pydantic and whole batches in bulk with Pandera: column types, required fields, value ranges, units (nM, µM, pIC50), duplicates, links between tables, and counts that agree across sources; measure why a million rows are not checked one at a time; stop or quarantine a batch that fails, and report why.

modules.title: Versioning everything
modules.what: Version code, environments, database schemas, standardisation rules, datasets and results, so any number can be traced back and rebuilt exactly.

modules.title: Monitoring pipelines
modules.what: Structured logs, run history, counts in and out that must reconcile, throughput and error rates, freshness, drift in molecular properties, and alerts when something goes wrong.

modules.title: Capstone: a resumable, monitored pipeline over a large library
modules.what: Standardise, deduplicate, filter and fingerprint millions of molecules end to end; stop it halfway, resume it, version the output and show that every count reconciles.

series.title: The Modern Data Stack for Chemistry
series.tagline: Production tools for lab data: ingestion, warehousing, transformation and scheduling.
series.summary: The tools data teams use in industry, applied to chemistry: declarative ingestion, a fast local warehouse, version-controlled transformations with lineage, scheduled pipelines and dashboards for medicinal chemists.

modules.title: Designing a lab data architecture
modules.what: From folders and spreadsheets to a modular open-source stack.

modules.title: Declarative ingestion
modules.what: Load chemical APIs and lab exports incrementally, coping with changing schemas.

modules.title: A fast analytical warehouse
modules.what: Query millions of descriptors locally with DuckDB and Parquet.

modules.title: Transformations with lineage
modules.what: Version-controlled models joining structures with assay results.

modules.title: Scheduled pipelines
modules.what: Run standardisation and fingerprint updates automatically when new data arrives.

modules.title: Structure-activity dashboards
modules.what: Interactive views of structure-activity relationships for medicinal chemists.

series.title: Data Pipelines for Digital and Autonomous Chemistry
series.tagline: The data side of automated synthesis: from designed molecules to checked results.
series.summary: What it takes to move data safely between molecular design, robotic synthesis and analysis: checks before synthesis, reaction metadata, instrument data, pipeline monitoring and a small intake service.

modules.title: From design to make
modules.what: Why moving from a virtual library to robotic synthesis is a data problem.

modules.title: Checking molecules before synthesis
modules.what: An intake check for stereocentres, salts and unstable groups.

modules.title: Reaction and synthesis metadata
modules.what: Relational tables for conditions, building blocks, yields and purity.

modules.title: Instrument data back into the pipeline
modules.what: Parse LC-MS and NMR exports into structured tables to confirm what was made.

modules.title: Monitoring lab data pipelines
modules.what: Catch schema drift, missing readings and corrupted values before they reach a model.

modules.title: A chemical intake service
modules.what: Wrap the checks and structure previews in a small web API.

modules.title: Capstone: a closed-loop pipeline
modules.what: Validate targets, log metadata, check analytical results and update the dataset safely.

tracks.title: MLOps for Chemists
tracks.tagline: Machine-learning models for chemistry that can be reproduced, deployed and monitored.
tracks.summary: Training a model once is the easy part. This track covers what keeps models useful: reproducible training, experiment tracking, model registries, deployment, and watching for drift as new chemistry arrives. It builds on the data engineering track. The outline will be published here first.

tracks.title: Agentic AI in Chemistry
tracks.tagline: AI agents that plan, run and check chemistry work with tools and data.
tracks.summary: Agents that call tools, read data and act on results are only as good as the data and pipelines behind them. This track builds on the data engineering and MLOps tracks. The outline will be published here first.
